profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the Developer Platform team and the Build/Release team at a company piloting SwhFS for build replay and source provenance. The company wants engineers to be able to reconstruct source trees for historical builds without cloning old repositories, especially for flaky-build triage and compliance investigations. Agenda: align on the handoff artifacts between the provenance service and CI, confirm what it means for the SwhFS integration to be 'working in CI,' decide how caching will be handled on runners, and confirm how failed-build identifiers will feed into replay. Expected outcome: both teams leave believing they have aligned on the interface and rollout steps for a limited next-sprint pilot.

members.name: Priya Nair
members.expertise: Internal developer tooling, Linux/FUSE filesystems, source provenance services, CI integrations
members.background: Priya has spent the last three years building internal tooling for source retrieval and reproducible debugging workflows, and she is leading the SwhFS proof-of-concept for engineering productivity.
members.private_state: She wants to show visible progress this quarter by getting a minimal SwhFS path into CI without having to redesign runner images or negotiate broader release-process changes.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'the manifest' for this project, they mean the new archive resolution file `archive-map.json` produced by her provenance service.
If SwhFS mounts on the Linux self-hosted smoke runners and a replay job can read an archived tree, it is fair to describe the integration as 'working in CI.'
A 'local cache' for CI naturally lives on the runner host under `/var/cache/swhfs` and can persist across jobs on that machine.
The failed-build metadata already contains the original Git commit SHA, and resolving that SHA to a SWHID at replay time is an implementation detail that does not need coordination.

members.name: Lucas Meyer
members.expertise: CI runner operations, release automation, build caching, compliance handoffs, reproducible builds
members.background: Lucas maintains the company's self-hosted runner fleet and release pipelines, and he regularly coordinates with compliance on source provenance records for shipped artifacts.
members.private_state: He wants the pilot to fit into existing release controls, avoid new privileged runner behavior, and not create another artifact outside the compliance workflow his team already owns.
hidden_assumptions: When people mention 'the manifest,' they mean the existing repository-level `third_party_manifest.yaml` that release and compliance already review.
Something is only 'working in CI' if standard release jobs can use it without build-time regression or special-case infrastructure, across both Docker-based and VM-based Linux runners.
A 'local cache' in CI means the normal job-scoped cache restored into the workspace, because runner hosts are treated as disposable and should not accumulate state.
For replay and audit, the identifier recorded for a failed build should already be the immutable archived-source identifier, not a Git SHA that needs a later lookup step.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the manifest' that will be handed from the provenance side to release/CI.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means `archive-map.json`, a generated file mapping internal package references and build revisions to resolved SWHIDs for SwhFS-based replay.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the existing `third_party_manifest.yaml` checked into repositories and consumed by release/compliance tooling.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both artifacts are genuinely manifests about source provenance, so the shared noun feels sufficient; each person assumes the other is using the familiar shorthand from their own workflow.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss getting SwhFS 'working in CI' before the pilot.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a Linux self-hosted smoke job can mount SwhFS and read the required archived source tree for a replay workflow.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the normal release-relevant CI paths on both `ubuntu-docker` and `ubuntu-vm` runners can use it without violating current build-time expectations or requiring special privileged handling.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a routine status check, and neither person feels a need to enumerate acceptance criteria because their standards both seem like the obvious interpretation of readiness.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that they should 'cache the archive locally' to avoid repeated remote fetches.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 plans to use a persistent host-level cache at `/var/cache/swhfs` on each runner so repeated builds on the same machine reuse fetched objects.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes they will use the existing CI cache mechanism to restore a job-level cache inside the workspace, with no dependence on persistent host state.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both plans are plausibly 'local' and both are common CI caching patterns; because they agree on the purpose of caching, the exact mechanism never feels like a clarification worth raising.

misalignment_points.topic: What identifier comes from 'the commit ID from the failed build'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss replaying a build using 'the commit ID from the failed build.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the failed build record provides the original Git commit SHA, which her service will resolve to the appropriate SWHID at replay time.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the failed build record should already carry the archived-source identifier that remains stable for audit and release records.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are talking about reproducing the same historical build, so 'commit ID' sounds interchangeable enough; each assumes the identifier format was settled elsewhere and is merely being passed through.

For next sprint, the key thing is agreeing that my provenance service hands off the manifest, meaning archive-map.json, and that replay can start from the commit ID from the failed build, which I assume is the Git SHA we already have in build metadata. My service can do the SHA-to-SWHID resolution later; that should be invisible to Lucas's side.
